ai.description: *Xylophis captaini* is a small, slender snake reaching 30–40 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct pale, dark-edged collar and a blunt, shovel-shaped snout adapted for burrowing in leaf litter.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Xylophis captaini* is best distinguished by its unique head pattern, featuring a distinct dark, V-shaped mark on the nape that is absent in other Indian wood snakes.
ai.habitat: *Xylophis captaini* inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Captain's Wood Snake is primarily nocturnal and specialized for foraging, often using its snout to probe leaf litter and soil for earthworms and soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Xylophis captaini* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Xylophis captaini* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,300 meters.
